Use Tier 2: add self-supervised graph contrastive regularization to the existing LightGCN expert, focusing on model_design and training_evaluation. This is one controlled change: retain SASRec, sampled-softmax ranking, learned graph-depth weights, history scoring, and the existing fusion grid. The latest macro HR@10 of 0.5938 remains below the best 0.5950, while Electronics stays at 0.4200, suggesting that improving collaborative representations deserves a controlled experiment.

During each graph training step, create two independently edge-dropped views of the training-only user–item graph, dropping 10% of undirected interactions and retaining both directions together. Recompute degree normalization for each view, encode both with shared LightGCN parameters, and apply an InfoNCE loss between matching users and matching items represented in the batch. Deduplicate batch identities before contrastive comparison so repeated users or items do not become false negatives. Use normalized embeddings, temperature 0.2, and a fixed auxiliary-loss coefficient of 0.05; keep the ranking objective on the complete training graph.

This targets sensitivity to individual interactions and sparse collaborative neighborhoods by encouraging consistent representations across perturbed graph views. Export embeddings from the complete training graph, preserving the existing predictor writer, dataset routing, and identical validation and inference scoring. Select checkpoints using the same fixed validation cases and HR@10 definition, report the four-category macro-average, and enforce the run deadline while accounting for the additional graph passes. Leave the supplied splits, seed settings, DATA_DIR, and host evaluation unchanged; do not access hidden test files or generate a submission from unavailable test samples.
